findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time, not per instance
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a plain dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created without an explicit `queued` gets that same stale timestamp, so the field does not record when the assignment was queued. If anything later uses `queued` for ordering, staleness or debugging, it will see wrong data. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. The `test_to_dict` test only asserts `queued is not None`, so it passes despite this bug.

findings.title: `to_dict` puts a raw `datetime` into Celery task kwargs; `from_dict` does not validate it
findings.body: `asdict(self)` leaves `queued` as a `datetime`, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes the result straight into `apply_async` kwargs. This only works while the broker serializer can handle datetimes, such as pickle. With a JSON serializer it would fail at enqueue time. `from_dict` also accepts any value for `queued` (for example an ISO string after a JSON round trip) and returns a source whose field has the wrong type. The cycle-breaking check only needs `integration_id`, so `queued` adds a serialization risk for no current use.

findings.title: Unused `assignment_source` parameter added to abstract `sync_status_outbound`
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` parameter, but nothing in this PR passes it and no implementation uses it. The PR only deals with assignee sync, so this widens the abstract contract with dead API surface. It also suggests status-sync cycles are handled when they are not. It should be removed, or actually wired up and tested.

findings.title: No test covers the inbound path that supplies the `AssignmentSource`
findings.body: The cycle fix depends on `sync_group_assignee_inbound` passing `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` to `assign`/`deassign`. The added tests only call `GroupAssignee.objects.assign` with a hand-built source. The existing inbound tests (`test_assignee_sync_inbound_assign` and `_deassign`) do not assert that outbound sync is suppressed. Removing the `assignment_source=` argument in `sync.py` would therefore break the fix without failing any test. There is also no test that an assignment from integration A is still propagated to integration B, and none for the deassign-with-source case or the task-level parsing of `assignment_source_dict`.
